draft.title: Plea negotiations
card: A plea is the accused's answer to a charge. A guilty plea admits the offence, so there is no trial on guilt and the court moves to sentencing. A not guilty plea sends the case to trial, where the prosecution must prove it.

In plea negotiations, the prosecution and defence talk before the trial. The accused agrees to plead guilty, often to a lesser charge or fewer charges. In return, the prosecution drops the other charges. In Victoria, the Office of Public Prosecutions conducts the talks.
It saves time and cost, and the court does not need a full trial. Witnesses, including victims, may not have to give evidence. This supports efficiency in the justice system.

It can raise concerns about fairness. The accused may be convicted of a lesser offence than the victim believes was committed, and the sentence may be lighter. The Office of Public Prosecutions must consider the victim's views under the Victims' Charter Act 2006 (Vic).
draft.remember: Plea negotiations trade a guilty plea for fewer or lesser charges. They save time and cost but can cut against fairness for victims.

a.q: In a plea negotiation, what does the accused usually agree to do?
opts: Plead guilty in return for fewer or lesser charges
Plead not guilty to every charge so the case goes on
Stay silent and ask the judge to dismiss the case
Plead guilty to all charges in return for a jury trial
a.why: In plea negotiations the accused gives a guilty plea. In return, the prosecution drops some charges or accepts a lesser one. Pleading not guilty to every charge sends the case to trial, so nothing is negotiated.
a.clue: The accused gives something up and gets something back.

b.q: Dev faces two charges. In plea negotiations he pleads guilty to one and the other is dropped. The victim, Sam, says the outcome lacks fairness. What is the most likely reason?
opts: Dev is convicted of less than Sam believes he did
Dev must face a full jury trial on both charges
Sam must give evidence for several days at a trial
Dev's guilty plea means the court cannot sentence him
b.why: Dev is convicted of only one offence, though Sam believes he committed both. The outcome does not match what Sam thinks happened. A full trial is wrong because a guilty plea avoids a trial on guilt.
b.clue: Think about what the dropped charge means for the outcome.

a.best: Plead guilty in return for fewer or lesser charges

b.best: Dev is convicted of less than Sam believes he did

problems.detail: "In Victoria, the Office of Public Prosecutions conducts the talks" is too absolute. The OPP negotiates for indictable matters in the higher courts, but Victoria Police prosecutors also conduct plea negotiations, for example in the Magistrates' Court. It should say the OPP conducts them for serious (indictable) cases.

check.summary: Both questions are sound, with one clearly correct answer each. The card overstates that the OPP conducts all plea negotiations in Victoria, when police prosecutors also do so in summary matters.
